page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance built on the ARMv9 architecture using AWS Neoverse-V2 cores. The system delivers 192 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.7 GHz with a single execution thread per core, eliminating hyper-threading contention. The processor architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core, backed by 36 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory comprises 384.0 GB of DDR5 RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per core compute-focused ratio. High-throughput local storage is integrated with 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, supported by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth characteristics. In synthetic multi-core evaluations, the server achieved 301,158.24 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 1,322.41 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, both placing in the top ten percent. High-speed memory subsystems reached 14,229.26 GB/sec for small cached reads and 909.18 GB/sec for large 256 MB uncached reads. In transactional and caching benchmarks, the platform generated 383.07 million Redis SET operations per second and 144.2 GB/sec in static web throughput. Single-core performance sits in the middle tier, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1,670.0 and stress-ng single-core reaching 1,648.6. Without dedicated matrix hardware or GPUs, text generation on 70B LLM models remains low at 2.31 tokens per second.

Eliminating hypervisor overhead via bare-metal access maximizes per-core throughput and predictable I/O latency. The high physical core count combined with 11.4 TB of local NVMe SSD storage makes the platform cost-efficient for scale-out parallel computing rather than single-threaded bottlenecks. Prime workload fits include continuous integration pipelines, software compilation with Clang, distributed database clusters, in-memory caching systems, physics simulations, and heavy multi-threaded compression tasks. Workloads dependent on x86 vector extensions or discrete GPU acceleration are unsuited to this platform.

The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, alongside 11,400 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded compute capability, highlighted by high scores in multi-core stress testing, 86,432.0 in Clang compilation, and 383.07 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 909.18 GB/sec on uncached reads. Single-core metrics remain average, and text generation on large language models is constrained due to the lack of hardware accelerators.
